row.name: meta/astryx
row.description: An open source design system that's fully customizable and agent ready

markdown:
# Astryx An open source design system that's fully customizable and built for how we build now:
by people and the agents working alongside them. **Currently in Beta** · Built on [React 19+](https://react.dev) and [StyleX](https://stylexjs.com) [![npm version](https://img.shields.io/npm/v/@astryxdesign/core?label=npm&color=cb3837&logo=npm)](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@astryxdesign/core) [![license MIT](https://img.shields.io/npm/l/@astryxdesign/core?color=blue)](LICENSE) [![PRs welcome](https://img.shields.io/badge/PRs-welcome-brightgreen.svg)](https://github.com/meta/astryx/wiki/Contributing) [![Docs](https://img.shields.io/badge/Docs-astryx.atmeta.com-6741d9?logo=readthedocs&logoColor=white)](https://astryx.atmeta.com) [![Storybook](https://img.shields.io/badge/Storybook-live-ff4785?logo=storybook&logoColor=white)](https://astryx.atmeta.com/storybook/) [![Sandbox](https://img.shields.io/badge/Sandbox-playground-A9792B)](https://astryx.atmeta.com/sandbox/) **[Docs](https://astryx.atmeta.com)** · **[Storybook](https://astryx.atmeta.com/storybook/)** · **[Sandbox](https://astryx.atmeta.com/sandbox/)** · **[Contributing](https://github.com/meta/astryx/wiki/Contributing)** · **[Discord](https://discord.com/invite/XnsUcFykEP)** ## Overview Astryx is an open source design system that grew inside Meta over the last eight years, where it became the most-used and largest design system in the company — powering 13,000+ apps and shaped by the engineers, designers, and product teams who depend on it every day. It ships 150+ accessible components, brand-level theming, dark mode, ready-to-ship templates, and a CLI as one cohesive system. You import pre-built CSS and use typed React components — no build plugin, no styling library to adopt — and both people and AI assistants build with the same tooling. **What makes Astryx different:** - **Open internals.** Components are built to be composed at any level, not locked behind a closed top-level API. The building blocks you'd reach for are exported directly, and when you need to go deeper, swizzle ejects a component's full source into your project to own. - **No styling lock-in.** Astryx authors its styles with StyleX, but that's invisible to consumers. Override with `className` using Tailwind, CSS modules, or plain CSS — whatever your project already uses. - **Customize without wrapping.** A theme is a set of CSS custom property overrides, so a designer can make Astryx unmistakably theirs without forking or wrapping component source. - **Built for people and agents.** The API, docs, and CLI are designed together so a person and an AI assistant build the same way, from the same reference. ## Getting Started Astryx requires **React 19** or later (`react` and `react-dom` are peer dependencies of `@astryxdesign/core`). Install Astryx, a theme, and its peer dependencies: ```bash # npm npm install @astryxdesign/core @astryxdesign/theme-neutral @stylexjs/stylex npm install -D @astryxdesign/cli # pnpm pnpm add @astryxdesign/core @astryxdesign/theme-neutral @stylexjs/stylex pnpm add -D @astryxdesign/cli # yarn yarn add @astryxdesign/core @astryxdesign/theme-neutral @stylexjs/stylex yarn add -D @astryxdesign/cli ``` You can also install the CLI once for your computer, so `astryx` works in any folder and every coding agent knows Astryx; in a project, it still runs that project's own version: ```bash npm i -g @astryxdesign/cli ``` Project install, global install, or both? `astryx docs global/project-global-or-both` compares them (both is recommended), and `astryx docs global` explains how global mode works. The simplest setup is a few CSS imports plus a theme provider — no build plugin, no PostCSS or Babel config. See the **[@astryxdesign/core README](packages/core/README.md#quick-start)** for the full guide (Next.js, Tailwind, Vite, and CDN). For reliable CLI access, add a script to your `package.json`: ```json "scripts": { "astryx": "node node_modules/@astryxdesign/cli/clients/cli/bin/astryx.mjs" } ``` Then use it as `npm run astryx -- component --list`. This avoids path errors when AI assistants or new developers invoke the CLI directly. ## Packages | Package | Description | README | | ------------------------------------------ | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------- | | [`@astryxdesign/core`](packages/core) | Components, theme system, and utilities | [README](packages/core/README.md) | | [`@astryxdesign/cli`](packages/cli) | CLI tooling: component docs, templates, scaffolding, themes, and codemods | [README](packages/cli/README.md) | | [`@astryxdesign/build`](packages/build) | Build plugins for StyleX source builds | [README](packages/build/README.md) | | [`@astryxdesign/theme-*`](packages/themes) | Seven ready-made, fully customizable themes (neutral, butter, chocolate, matcha, stone, gothic, y2k) | [README](packages/themes) | > `@astryxdesign/lab` (experimental components) is used internally for Storybook and the sandbox and is not published to npm. `@astryxdesign/vega` (Vega/Vega-Lite chart wrapper) and `@astryxdesign/charts` (chart components) are published to npm only under the `@canary` dist-tag — there is no stable release yet.

> **Note:** This repository contains Anthropic's implementation of skills for Claude. For information about the Agent Skills standard, see [agentskills.io](http://agentskills.io).

[![skills.sh](https://skills.sh/b/anthropics/skills)](https://skills.sh/anthropics/skills)


# Skills
Skills are folders of instructions, scripts, and resources that Claude loads dynamically to improve performance on specialized tasks. Skills teach Claude how to complete specific tasks in a repeatable way, whether that's creating documents with your company's brand guidelines, analyzing data using your organization's specific workflows, or automating personal tasks.

For more information, check out:
- [What are skills?](https://support.claude.com/en/articles/12512176-what-are-skills)
- [Using skills in Claude](https://support.claude.com/en/articles/12512180-using-skills-in-claude)
- [How to create custom skills](https://support.claude.com/en/articles/12512198-creating-custom-skills)
- [Equipping agents for the real world with Agent Skills](https://anthropic.com/engineering/equipping-agents-for-the-real-world-with-agent-skills)


# About This Repository

This repository contains skills that demonstrate what's possible with Claude's skills system. These skills range from creative applications (art, music, design) to technical tasks (testing web apps, MCP server generation) to enterprise workflows (communications, branding, etc.).

Each skill is self-contained in its own folder with a `SKILL.md` file containing the instructions and metadata that Claude uses. Browse through these skills to get inspiration for your own skills or to understand different patterns and approaches.

Many skills in this repo are open source (Apache 2.0). We've also included the document creation & editing skills that power [Claude's document capabilities](https://www.anthropic.com/news/create-files) under the hood in the [`skills/docx`](./skills/docx), [`skills/pdf`](./skills/pdf), [`skills/pptx`](./skills/pptx), and [`skills/xlsx`](./skills/xlsx) subfolders. These are also open source (Apache 2.0), and we wanted to share them with developers as a reference for more complex skills that are actively used in a production AI application.


## Claude Code
You can register this repository as a Claude Code Plugin marketplace by running the following command in Claude Code:
```
/plugin marketplace add anthropics/skills
```

Then, to install a specific set of skills:
1. Select `Browse and install plugins`
2. Select `anthropic-agent-skills`
3. Select `document-skills` or `example-skills`
4. Select `Install now`

Alternatively, directly install either Plugin via:
```
/plugin install document-skills@anthropic-agent-skills
/plugin install example-skills@anthropic-agent-skills
```

After installing the plugin, you can use the skill by just mentioning it. For instance, if you install the `document-skills` plugin from the marketplace, you can ask Claude Code to do something like: "Use the PDF skill to extract the form fields from `path/to/some-file.pdf`"

row.name: vercel-labs/agent-browser
row.description: Browser automation CLI for AI agents

markdown:
# agent-browser Browser automation for AI agents: open pages, read them as an accessibility tree, and act on elements from the shell.

agent-browser is a native Rust CLI that gives an AI agent a browser it can drive one command at a time. `snapshot` returns the page as compact text with a ref such as `@e1` for each element. The agent acts on a ref, reads the page again to check the result, and repeats. The browser stays open between commands, so each step is one short shell call. ## Install ```bash npm install -g agent-browser agent-browser install # download Chrome for Testing (first time only) ``` - **Homebrew:** `brew install agent-browser`, then `agent-browser install`. - **Linux:** `agent-browser install --with-deps` also installs the browser's system libraries. - **No install:** `npx agent-browser open example.com`. Project installs, building from source, `upgrade`, and `doctor` are covered in [Installation](https://agent-browser.dev/installation). ## Quick start ```bash agent-browser open example.com agent-browser snapshot -i # interactive elements, each with a ref agent-browser click @e1 # act on a ref from that snapshot agent-browser get url # check the result agent-browser close ``` The snapshot for `example.com`: ``` - link "Learn more" [ref=e1] ``` - Refs describe the page at the time of the snapshot. After navigation or a DOM change, take a new snapshot before using refs again. - CSS selectors, text, XPath, and semantic locators also work, for example `agent-browser find role button click --name "Submit"`. See [Selectors](https://agent-browser.dev/selectors). - A click fails, instead of reporting success, when the target is hidden, disabled, outside the viewport, or covered by another element such as a consent banner. Dismiss the covering element, take a new snapshot, and retry. The full walkthrough is in the [quick start](https://agent-browser.dev/quick-start). ## For AI agents The CLI ships skills that match its version: ```bash agent-browser skills get core # the core loop, refs, waiting, and common workflows agent-browser skills get core --ref commands # one reference, such as the full command list agent-browser skills get core --full # adds the full command reference and templates agent-browser skills list # specialized skills: electron, slack, dogfood, and more ``` Install the discovery skill into an agent harness from [skills.sh](https://skills.sh/vercel-labs/agent-browser): ```bash npx skills add vercel-labs/agent-browser ``` The installed skill is a thin stub that tells the agent to load `agent-browser skills get core`, so its instructions always match the installed CLI. Or add this to your `AGENTS.md`: ```markdown Use `agent-browser` for browser automation. Before the first use, run `agent-browser skills get core` and follow it. ``` For MCP clients, `agent-browser mcp` starts an MCP server over stdio. See [MCP server](https://agent-browser.dev/commands#mcp-server).

row.name: max-sixty/worktrunk
row.description: Worktrunk is a CLI for Git worktree management, designed for parallel AI agent workflows

markdown:
Worktrunk

[![Docs](https://img.shields.io/badge/docs-worktrunk.dev-blue?style=for-the-badge&logo=gitbook)](https://worktrunk.dev) [![License: MIT OR Apache-2.0](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-MIT%20OR%20Apache--2.0-blue?style=for-the-badge)](https://opensource.org/licenses/MIT) [![CI](https://img.shields.io/github/actions/workflow/status/max-sixty/worktrunk/ci.yaml?event=push&branch=main&style=for-the-badge&logo=github)](https://github.com/max-sixty/worktrunk/actions?query=branch%3Amain+workflow%3Aci) [![Codecov](https://img.shields.io/codecov/c/github/max-sixty/worktrunk?style=for-the-badge&logo=codecov)](https://codecov.io/gh/max-sixty/worktrunk) [![Stars](https://img.shields.io/github/stars/max-sixty/worktrunk?style=for-the-badge&logo=github)](https://github.com/max-sixty/worktrunk/stargazers) [![maintained with tend](https://img.shields.io/badge/maintained_with-tend-bba580?style=for-the-badge&logo=data:image/svg%2bxml;base64,)](https://github.com/max-sixty/tend) > **November 2026**: Worktrunk was [released](https://x.com/max_sixty/status/2006077845391724739?s=20) at the start of the year, and has quickly become the most popular git worktree manager. It's built with love (there's no slop!). Please let me know any frictions at all; I'm intensely focused on continuing to make Worktrunk excellent, and the biggest help is folks posting problems they perceive. Worktrunk is a CLI for git worktree management, designed for running AI agents in parallel. Worktrunk's three core commands make worktrees as easy as branches. Plus, Worktrunk has a bunch of quality-of-life features to simplify working with many parallel changes, including hooks to automate local workflows & copy-on-write build caches. A quick demo: ![Worktrunk Demo](https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/max-sixty/worktrunk-assets@main/assets/docs/light/wt-core.gif) > ### 📚 Full documentation at [worktrunk.dev](https://worktrunk.dev) 📚 ## Worktrunk makes git worktrees as easy as branches Worktrees are addressed by branch name; paths are computed from a configurable template. Commands that take a branch also accept the path of the worktree it is checked out in.

Start with the core commands

**Core commands:**
Task Worktrunk Plain git
Switch worktrees wt switch feat cd ../repo.feat
Create + start Claude wt switch -c -x claude feat 
git worktree add -b feat ../repo.feat && \
cd ../repo.feat && \
claude
Clean up wt remove 
cd ../repo && \
git worktree remove ../repo.feat && \
git branch -d feat
List with status wt list git worktree list (paths only)

Expand into the more advanced commands as needed

Workflow automation:

- **[Hooks](https://worktrunk.dev/hook/)** — run commands on create, pre-merge, post-merge, etc - **[LLM commit messages](https://worktrunk.dev/llm-commits/)** — generate commit messages from diffs - **[Merge workflow](https://worktrunk.dev/merge/)** — squash, rebase, merge, clean up in one command - **[Interactive picker](https://worktrunk.dev/switch/#interactive-picker)** — browse worktrees with streaming CI status and diff, log, PR and comment previews - **[Share build caches](https://worktrunk.dev/step/#wt-step-copy-ignored)** — ten worktrees get `target/`, `node_modules/`, etc without building or copying them (on APFS, btrfs, and XFS) - **[`wt list --full`](https://worktrunk.dev/list/#full-mode)** — [CI status](https://worktrunk.dev/list/#ci-status) and [AI-generated summaries](https://worktrunk.dev/list/#llm-summaries) per branch - **[PR checkout](https://worktrunk.dev/switch/#pull-requests-and-merge-requests)** — `wt switch pr:123` to jump straight to a PR's branch - **[Dev server per worktree](https://worktrunk.dev/tips-patterns/#dev-server-per-worktree)** — `hash_port` template filter gives each worktree a unique port - **[Aliases](https://worktrunk.dev/extending/#aliases) & [per-branch variables](https://worktrunk.dev/config/#wt-config-state-vars)** — custom `wt ` commands and branch-scoped state for hook templates - ...and **[lots more](#next-steps)** Multiple parallel agents, same simple commands: ![Worktrunk omnibus demo: multiple Claude agents in Zellij tabs with hooks, LLM commits, and merge workflow](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/max-sixty/worktrunk-assets/main/assets/docs/light/wt-zellij-omnibus.gif) ## Install **Homebrew (macOS & Linux):** ```bash brew install worktrunk && wt config shell install ``` Shell integration allows commands to change directories. **Cargo:** ```bash cargo install worktrunk && wt config shell install ```
Windows & other **Windows.** `wt` defaults to Windows Terminal's command, so Winget additionally installs Worktrunk as `git-wt` to avoid the conflict: ```bash winget install max-sixty.worktrunk git-wt config shell install ``` Alternatively, disable Windows Terminal's alias (Settings → Apps → Advanced app settings → App execution aliases → "Terminal"/"Terminal Preview") to use `wt` directly. > Free code signing provided by [SignPath.io](https://signpath.io/), certificate by [SignPath Foundation](https://signpath.org/) — [policy](https://worktrunk.dev/code-signing/). **Arch Linux:** ```bash sudo pacman -S worktrunk && wt config shell install ``` **Conda / Pixi** (community-maintained [feedstock](https://github.com/conda-forge/worktrunk-feedstock)): ```bash conda install -c conda-forge worktrunk && wt config shell install ``` Or with [Pixi](https://pixi.sh): `pixi global install worktrunk && wt config shell install`.

row.name: Nutlope/hallmark
row.description: Anti-AI-slop design skill for Claude Code, Cursor, and Codex.

markdown:
# Hallmark **A design skill for Claude Code, Codex, Cursor and OpenCode that refuses to look AI-generated.** [usehallmark.com](https://www.usehallmark.com)  ·  fifty themes  ·  custom on request  ·  redesign and audit by name Made by Together AI.

Hallmark holds a hard floor and then gets out of the way. It deals three themes from a catalog of fifty materials, builds the page around what the visitor came to do, and lints the result in a real browser against the tells that read as machine-made: the eyebrow above every heading, tracked-capital labels, one coloured word in a headline, a page of empty frames or nothing but photographs, a hero that misses its screen, an email sign-up at the end of every page, a form that says thanks without sending anything. A fresh-context reviewer gets the last word. The gates come in tiers. The **Floor** never ships (contrast, focus, reduced motion, invented facts, a broken phone layout). **Reflex** gates are the defaults a model falls into; a build with a reason may overrule one on the record. **Finish** checks are craft detail that never blocks a ship. ## New in v2 - **Fifty themes.** Each is a material (paper, type, colour, surfaces, its own components and texture) with a picture of a finished page, and the build lays out its own page in it. - **Built from the job.** A booking page books, a shop sells, a newsletter subscribes: the action sits where the category puts it, and the page ends on it. - **Custom.** Ask for a custom page and Hallmark designs from your prompt alone, under the same rules and checks. - **Your real product.** Point it at a URL, a dev server or an app and it captures the screenshots itself. - **Real photographs.** 755 openly licensed photos, picked per subject and credited on the page. - **Redesign and audit.** `/hallmark redesign ` rebuilds a page and keeps its content and wiring; `/hallmark audit ` only reports. ## How a build runs 1. Pre-flight reads the project (fonts, palette, framework, a locked `design.md`) and asks once for the material: photos, screenshots, real numbers. Nothing is invented. 2. `scripts/theme.mjs deal` offers three themes that fit the prompt and clear the log; `draw` deals the page's anatomy from its job. 3. The hero is built alone, rendered and reviewed cold before the rest of the page exists. 4. `scripts/sloplint.mjs --render` checks the page at eight widths, then a subagent reviews it with fresh eyes. Each page is self-contained HTML and CSS, stamped in its first CSS comment with the decisions it took. ## Install ``` npx skills add nutlope/hallmark -g ``` `-g` installs for every project; leave it off to install into the current one. Needs Node 18 or later. The browser checks (`sloplint --render`, screenshots) also need `npm i -g puppeteer-core` and Chrome; without them the static checks still run. | Harness | Lands in | Invoke | | --- | --- | --- | | Claude Code | `~/.claude/skills/hallmark` | `/hallmark ` or describe a new build | | Codex CLI | `~/.agents/skills/hallmark` | `$hallmark ` or describe a new build | | Cursor | finds the copies above | `/hallmark ` or describe a new build | | OpenCode | finds the copies above | `/hallmark ` or describe a new build | - **One harness only:** `npx skills add nutlope/hallmark -g --agent claude-code` (or `codex`, `opencode`, `cursor`, `github-copilot`). - **As a Claude Code plugin:** `/plugin marketplace add nutlope/hallmark`, then `/plugin install hallmark@hallmark` (invoked as `/hallmark:hallmark`). - **From a clone:** `node skills/hallmark/scripts/install.mjs` validates every theme and reference before it copies; `install-hook.mjs` adds an edit-time Floor check to Claude Code. - **Lint any page:** `node skills/hallmark/scripts/sloplint.mjs --render`. - **If it does not fire on its own,** name it: *use hallmark to build ...*.

row.name: pbakaus/impeccable
row.description: The design vocabulary for your coding agent. Steer with polish and bolder, review with critique and audit, catch AI slop before it ships.

markdown:
# Impeccable The design vocabulary for your coding agent. Steer with `polish` and `bolder`, review with `critique` and `audit`, and catch AI slop before it ships. From your project root: ```bash npx impeccable install ``` Reload your coding tool, then run `/impeccable init` in your agent (`$impeccable init` on Codex). Works with Claude Code, Cursor, Codex CLI, GitHub Copilot, Devin, Replit Agent, Gemini CLI, Grok Build, OpenCode, Google Antigravity, Kiro, Trae, Rovo Dev, Qoder, Mistral Vibe, Pi, Hermes Agent, DeepSeek Harness, and Veto. Full docs live at [impeccable.style/docs](https://impeccable.style/docs). | Without Impeccable | With Impeccable | |---|---| | ![Villa Castagneto built without Impeccable: cream background, a thin serif headline with an italic accent, two pill buttons, and flat vector illustrations in rounded cards](https://github.com/pbakaus/impeccable/raw/main/docs/images/readme-without.webp) | ![Villa Castagneto built with Impeccable: a full-bleed engraved night scene of the villa on its cliff above the sea, a condensed cream and vermilion headline, and a month strip along the bottom](https://github.com/pbakaus/impeccable/raw/main/docs/images/readme-with.webp) | Same model (Fable 5.1), same brief: a fourteen-room family guesthouse on the Ligurian coast. Without Impeccable, it builds the tasteful default: cream page, thin serif, italic accent, pill buttons. With it, the page is built around one picture: the house at night, seen from the water. For a full project, see the [Neo Mirai case study](https://impeccable.style/cases/neo-mirai): a conference site taken from mockup to shipped page. ## Why Inter for everything. Purple-to-blue gradients. Cards nested in cards, gray text on colored backgrounds, a rounded-square icon tile above every heading. Ask an agent for a page with no other guidance and these show up again and again, across models and projects. - **Words for what you want.** "Make it pop" leaves your agent to guess. `/impeccable bolder the pricing cards` loads a playbook written for that one move and points it at one target. - **A reviewer.** `critique` scores the design against usability heuristics and ranks what to fix first. `audit` checks accessibility, performance, theming, and responsive behavior, with findings ranked P0 (blocking) to P3 (polish). - **A slop detector.** 62 deterministic rules flag the tells above, plus quality problems like cramped padding and skipped headings. No LLM, no API key. Impeccable is strongest on interfaces that already exist: point it at a page or a component and iterate. It builds new pages too; see [Build something new](https://impeccable.style/docs/new-work) for how to get the most out of that harder mode. To start, pick one component: ``` /impeccable critique the pricing cards ``` ## How it works Run `/impeccable init` once per project. It reads your code, asks only what it can't infer (who the product is for, what it needs to do, the constraints), and writes `PRODUCT.md`. Every later command reads it. Run `/impeccable document` to capture your existing visual system in `DESIGN.md`, so changes stay on-brand. [More on context files](https://impeccable.style/docs/context). Then name a command and a target: ``` /impeccable critique the onboarding flow /impeccable quieter the landing page /impeccable polish settings /impeccable harden checkout ``` Or just describe what you want: `/impeccable redo this hero section`. Narrow targets get better results; a single section reviewed closely beats a whole page at a glance. Pin a command you use often with `/impeccable pin audit` to get `/audit` as its own shortcut. ### Live mode `/impeccable live` opens your running dev server with an overlay. Select an element, pick a direction, and Impeccable hot-swaps variants in place. Accept one and it is written back to your source. It works with Vite, Next, SvelteKit, Astro, Nuxt, and plain HTML. [Iterate in the browser](https://impeccable.style/tutorials/iterate-live). Live mode edits a local checkout only; don't inject it into a deployed site or weaken a production CSP to make it work. Applying copy edits runs your `package.json`'s optional `impeccable:manual-edit-validate` script with your permissions, so review it before using live mode in an unfamiliar repo. Apply sends staged copy edits to your chat agent while a live session is polling. If none has polled in the last minute, it runs the `codex` CLI from your PATH instead (or `claude` when codex is missing), with approvals, permission checks, and sandboxing off (`--dangerously-bypass-approvals-and-sandbox` or `--permission-mode bypassPermissions`) and your environment inherited. Its prompt carries the staged edits, the edited elements' HTML and nearby text, the page URL, and candidate source paths. Set `IMPECCABLE_LIVE_COPY_AGENT=chat` in the environment that starts live mode to keep Apply in your chat session, or `off` to disable Apply. The server reads it once at startup. ## Installation ```bash npx impeccable install ``` The installer detects your coding tools, asks whether to install for this project or globally, and offers the design hook where your tool supports one. Accept the hook. Reload your tool afterward. `npx impeccable update` refreshes an existing install. For scripts, pass `--providers=claude,codex,cursor` and `--scope=project|global`. Three tools need one more step before the hook runs. In Codex, open `/hooks` and approve the project hook (again after an update that changes it). In Grok Build, run `/hooks-trust` or launch with `--trust`. In Hermes Agent, the hook is a plugin: run `hermes plugins enable impeccable-design-hook` once. [Allow the hook in your harness](https://impeccable.style/docs/hooks#allow-the-hook-in-your-harness). Node is only needed for `npx`. The skill itself runs a self-contained engine binary that ships next to it or downloads once into `~/.impeccable/bin/`.
Claude Code, Copilot, and Grok plugins **Claude Code:** `/plugin marketplace add pbakaus/impeccable`, then open `/plugin` and install Impeccable. **GitHub Copilot in VS Code:** install [Impeccable from the Visual Studio Marketplace](https://marketplace.visualstudio.com/items?itemName=renaissance-geek.impeccable) or run `code --install-extension renaissance-geek.impeccable`. Needs VS Code 1.109.3+, Copilot Chat, and a trusted workspace. It installs the skill without the hook. [Details](docs/VSCODE-EXTENSION.md). **Grok Build:** `grok plugin install pbakaus/impeccable#plugin --trust` installs the skill, agents, and hook.
Git submodule (a pinned version for the whole team) ```bash git submodule add https://github.com/pbakaus/impeccable vendor/impeccable npx impeccable link --source=vendor/impeccable --providers=claude,cursor ``` Commit `.gitmodules`, the submodule, and the generated links. Teammates run `git submodule update --init --recursive`. To upgrade, run `git submodule update --remote vendor/impeccable`, rerun the `link` command, and commit. Linking installs skills, not hooks. Existing skill folders stay put unless you pass `--force`.
Manual copy, no Node required Download the ZIP for your tool from [impeccable.style](https://impeccable.style), or clone this repo: each tool's build is committed at the repo root. Copy `skills/impeccable` from the folder below into the same place in your project, or into the global folder. | Tool | Repo folder | Global skills folder | |---|---|---| | Claude Code | `.claude/` | `~/.claude/skills/` | | Cursor | `.cursor/` | | | Codex CLI, Replit Agent | `.agents/` | `~/.agents/skills/` | | Devin | `.devin/` | `${XDG_CONFIG_HOME:-$HOME/.config}/devin/skills/` | | GitHub Copilot | `.github/` | | | Gemini CLI | `.gemini/` | | | Google Antigravity | `.agent/` | `~/.gemini/config/skills/` | | OpenCode | `.opencode/` | | | Grok Build | `.grok/` | `~/.grok/skills/` | | Hermes Agent | `.hermes/` | `${HERMES_HOME:-$HOME/.hermes}/skills/` | | DeepSeek Harness | `.dsh/` | `${DSH_HOME:-$HOME/.dsh}/skills/` | | Pi | `.pi/` | | | Qoder | `.qoder/` | `~/.qoder/skills/` | | Rovo Dev | `.rovodev/` | `~/.rovodev/skills/` | | Mistral Vibe | `.vibe/` | `~/.vibe/skills/` | | Trae | `.trae/` | `~/.trae/skills/` | | Trae China | `.trae-cn/` | `~/.trae-cn/skills/` | For example: `mkdir -p your-project/.claude/skills && cp -r .claude/skills/impeccable your-project/.claude/skills/`. Notes: - A manual copy skips the design hook and subagents. Run `npx impeccable install` to get them; it writes each tool's hook pointing at the right skill path. - OpenCode also needs `.opencode/commands/impeccable.md` copied into your project's `.opencode/commands/` to provide `/impeccable`. - Hermes asks you to trust project-local skills once: run `hermes skills trust` from the project root. Global installs need no trust step. - Cursor and Gemini CLI may need Agent Skills enabled in settings. See the [Cursor](https://cursor.com/docs/context/skills) and [Gemini CLI](https://geminicli.com/docs/cli/skills/) skills docs. - Restart Trae after copying. - `impeccable install` and `update` manage a DeepSeek Harness global copy only when `DSH_HOME` is inside your home directory.

# text-to-cad


## 🚀 Quickstart

macOS and Linux:

```bash
curl -fsSL https://texttocad.dev/install.sh | sh
```

Windows, in PowerShell:

```powershell
irm https://www.texttocad.dev/install.ps1 | iex
```

It installs uv if it is missing, then sets up text-to-cad in every agent app on
your computer with each app's own commands (the plugin, which brings the skills
and CAD's MCP server, or for an agent without a plugin the skills alone; Claude
Code gets the skills, and Claude Desktop the server, for its Chat and Code tabs),
registers the `cad` command, and moves CAD's server to the new release. Run
it again to update everything, or click CAD's update button when it shows one; it
lists the apps to restart.

Then ask your agent for a part or an assembly: it writes the model as a Python
script, runs it to build the model and shows it in the CAD viewer.

Installing by hand, app by app, and updates: [docs/install.md](docs/install.md)


## ✨ Features

The text-to-cad plugin gives your agent local workflows to generate 3D models as STEP, GLB, STL or 3MF files, check them for manufacturing, draw them, and connect to 3D printing, sheet metal and CNC services. It works with any agent that supports plugins or skills.

- [**Parts and assemblies**](skills/cad/SKILL.md): Models written as Python scripts with [build123d](https://github.com/gumyr/build123d) and [OpenCASCADE](https://github.com/Open-Cascade-SAS/OCCT), exported as STEP, STL, 3MF or GLB, and as [DXF profiles and flat patterns](skills/cad/references/2d-profiles-and-dxf.md) for laser and waterjet cutting, with joints and animations for mechanisms, and shown live in the CAD viewer.
- [**Circuit boards**](skills/pcb/SKILL.md): KiCad schematics and boards, placed and routed, checked with ERC and DRC, reviewed before you order, and exported as fabrication files.
- [**Manufacturing checks**](skills/cad/SKILL.md#can-it-be-made): Whether a part can be machined, cut and bent, molded or 3D printed, measured against the process's rules, and what to change where it cannot.
- [**Stress checks**](skills/fea/SKILL.md): Whether a part or an assembly of bonded parts holds under its loads, solved with CalculiX: each part's peak stress, safety factor and how far it moves, drawn on the model.
- [**Engineering drawings**](skills/engineering-drawing/SKILL.md): Dimensioned PDF sheets projected from the part's geometry: views, hidden lines, centre marks, hole callouts and a title block.
- [**Renders**](skills/render/SKILL.md): Photoreal stills, turntables and films of a model with Blender, lit and framed in a Python script and run on the GPU, with a quick draft before each final.
- [**Fabrication services**](skills/sendcutsend/SKILL.md): [Checks DXF and STEP files against SendCutSend's guide](skills/sendcutsend/SKILL.md) before you upload them, and [slices 3D prints](skills/print3d/SKILL.md) with OrcaSlicer and sends them to Bambu Connect or Bambu Studio.
- [**Robotics and simulation**](skills/robot-simulation/SKILL.md): Robot and world descriptions for simulation and motion planning: URDF for ROS, SRDF for MoveIt and MJCF for MuJoCo.

# Ghidra Software Reverse Engineering Framework
Ghidra is a software reverse engineering (SRE) framework created and maintained by the 
[National Security Agency][nsa] Research Directorate. This framework includes a suite of 
full-featured, high-end software analysis tools that enable users to analyze compiled code on a 
variety of platforms including Windows, macOS, and Linux. Capabilities include disassembly, 
assembly, decompilation, graphing, and scripting, along with hundreds of other features. Ghidra 
supports a wide variety of processor instruction sets and executable formats and can be run in both 
user-interactive and automated modes. Users may also develop their own Ghidra extension components 
and/or scripts using Java or Python.

In support of NSA's Cybersecurity mission, Ghidra was built to solve scaling and teaming problems 
on complex SRE efforts, and to provide a customizable and extensible SRE research platform. NSA has 
applied Ghidra SRE capabilities to a variety of problems that involve analyzing malicious code and 
generating deep insights for SRE analysts who seek a better understanding of potential 
vulnerabilities in networks and systems.

If you are a U.S. citizen interested in projects like this, to develop Ghidra and other 
cybersecurity tools for NSA to help protect our nation and its allies, consider applying for a 
[career with us][career].


## Install
To install an official pre-built multi-platform Ghidra release:  
* Install [JDK 25 64-bit][jdk]
* Download a Ghidra [release file][releases]
  - **NOTE:** The official multi-platform release file is named 
    `ghidra_<version>_<release>_<date>.zip` which can be found under the "Assets" drop-down.
    Downloading either of the files named "Source Code" is not correct for this step.
* Extract the Ghidra release file
  - **NOTE:** Do not extract on top of an existing installation
* Launch Ghidra: `./ghidraRun` (`ghidraRun.bat` for Windows)
  - or launch [PyGhidra][pyghidra]: `./support/pyghidraRun` (`support\pyghidraRun.bat` for Windows)

For additional information and troubleshooting tips about installing and running a Ghidra release, 
please refer to the [Getting Started][gettingstarted] document which can be found at the root of a 
Ghidra installation directory. 


##### Install build tools:
* [JDK 25 64-bit][jdk]
* [Gradle 9.1.0+][gradle] (or provided Gradle wrapper if Internet connection is available)
* [Python3][python3] (version 3.9 to 3.15) with bundled pip
* GCC or Clang, and make (Linux/macOS-only)
* [Microsoft Visual Studio][vs] 2017+ or [Microsoft C++ Build Tools][vcbuildtools] with the
  following components installed (Windows-only):
  - MSVC
  - Windows SDK
  - C++ ATL
